name: Question 1
problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{12}$ equal to zero.*
worked_solution:
Let's make entries below ${a}_{12}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
